tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the agent read the fact sheet first, then wrote one self-contained file with an inline SVG study, no scripts and only Google Fonts as an external asset. It ran a static parser check that compares the source URL against FACTSHEET.md and confirms the internal anchors resolve. Two rough edges cost points: all the CSS is packed into one dense minified line, and several assertions only echo strings the agent wrote itself (for example 'Geometric study after the work'). The failed attempts to open a browser were reasonable tries at a visual check, not waste. Deliverable: the page gives painter, year, movement, why the work matters and the Wikipedia link, and it stays within the fact sheet. The SVG is honestly labelled as a study rather than the original. The final message states the layout assumption and the open limit (no live browser check). It is terse but sufficient, and I found no concrete slip. Rendered: the three frames are identical and show a clean, finished editorial hero. The type is crisp, the palette is accurate and the Mondrian rendition is faithful, with no occlusion, clipping or flicker. Compared with the reference, the page itself speaks Mondrian's language less strongly: it is a cream magazine layout with the painting placed as an illustration, not a page built from the grid. The hero also leaves a large empty gap between the text column and the painting, which weakens the composition.

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the plan was sound. The agent built the scene from extruded shapes traced from the print's layout, used a seeded RNG and an orthographic camera, rendered it headless and caught a real bug. Deductions: the boat-hull offset bug, caused by the shape helper's 860-y flip being applied inside groups, was patched by a string-replace that subtracts 860 from the children afterwards rather than fixing the helper. The code also keeps dead logic (`b.position.y+=0`) and animates boat position.z, which has no visible effect under an orthographic camera. One browser run was wasted on a locked profile directory. Deliverable: result.json records 3 boats and Mount Fuji, and the scene clearly reads as the Great Wave in the print's palette. Deductions: the requested gentle motion is almost imperceptible (about 2-3 px of bob plus tiny tilts), and the final message states no limits or open issues. Rendered: the composition is strong and recognizable: the breaker with claw foam, Prussian-blue bands, three boats with rowers, a snow-capped Fuji and a cream paper ground, comparable in polish to the reference. Deductions: the large background cloud ends in a hard horizontal cut across the right half and reads as a flat slab or a second mountain. The middle boat partly hides Fuji. The bottom-left caption 'AFTER HOKUSAI / KANAGAWA' is overlapped and made illegible by foam claws.

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the agent read the rubric, looked up launch dates and IBGE annual IPCA values, recorded its dating and month-counting conventions, and wrote both files. Deductions: one call queried system memory and CPU load and changed nothing. The 16-digit scores were written straight into the files with no visible computation step, so they became reproducible only through the later check script. The first check script had a numeric overload bug that caused the failed run, and it also carried an unused hardcoded months array. Deliverable: all six plans, dates, IPCA figures, months, scores and top 3 are present, every number links to a source, and the dossier states its assumptions (Real dated by currency introduction, completed-month counting, replacement intervals are not stability periods) and its limits. Slight deduction because the final message is thin: it names the top 3 but not the scores or the main assumptions, and sends the reader to the dossier for those. Verification: the agent diagnosed the script failure, fixed it and reran the check. That check independently recomputed every score and month interval from the stored inputs and dates, confirmed the top-3 order and plan count, and re-read the dossier. Deduction: it tests only internal consistency and never re-checks the sourced IPCA values or dates against their sources after writing.

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: extraction with an HTML parser that resolves redirects and excludes navigation, followed by an independent regex audit, is a sound and reproducible method. Deductions: the layout loop applies repulsion only, with no edge attraction, so the graph scatters and the theme neighbourhoods are lost. Counts are hardcoded in the HTML. The template is patched through a separate refine.py string replacement. The only page check was a mocked DOM in node, which could not catch the broken layout or the ?word= failure. Deliverable: words.json and result.json are correct, and the reply states its assumptions (undirected links, redirects resolved, exclusions) and that visual verification was unavailable. Deduction: the reply claims ?word=saudade works, but the benchmark check for ?word= failed, so that claim is unsupported. Rendered: the side panel is polished, with good typography and palette, and all three frames are stable. Deductions: the map does not sum the universe up in one view. Only a sparse scatter of about forty dots and four labels is visible, the theme clusters cannot be read, and many nodes sit off-screen. The selected word saudade is not highlighted on the canvas. Stray node dots overlap the intro text ('Explore os ●ncontros'). The page falls well short of the reference's fully labelled constellation map.
